verdict.rationale: OpenTofu documents itself as a drop-in replacement for Terraform that preserves existing workflows and configurations, and its loader reads `.tf` files alongside `.tofu`. Independent community reports describe migration as trivial ("s/terraform/opentofu/g"), and a consultancy says it has already moved clients over. Carrying over existing Terraform state is implied by "drop-in replacement" rather than explicitly documented; `tofu import` covers importing live resources, not Terraform state files. missing for 10: an explicit first-party migration guide, documented compatibility of Terraform state files and versions.

support.subject: As a platform-engineer, I can migrate an existing Terraform-format codebase and its state into this tool

citations.quote: It serves as a drop-in replacement for Terraform, preserving your existing workflows and configurations.
This ensures that `.tofu` files always take precedence over `.tf` files when both are available.
Fortunately using OpenTofu is just s/terraform/opentofu/g at this point.
A consultancy reported that OpenTofu is an easy migration.
